claims.claim: Average seawater salinity is about 3.5%, i.e. roughly 35 grams of dissolved salt per liter (35 kg per cubic meter).
claims.episode_span: Seawater contains roughly 35 kilograms of salt per cubic meter.
claims.supporting_quote: On average, seawater in the world's oceans has a salinity of about 3.5% (35 g/L, 35 ppt, 600 mM).

claims.claim: The thermodynamic minimum energy for seawater desalination is around 1 kWh per cubic meter, excluding prefiltering and intake/outfall pumping.
claims.episode_span: that floor sits near 1.0 to 1.1 kilowatt-hours per cubic meter of product water
claims.supporting_quote: A minimum energy consumption for seawater desalination of around 1 kWh/m 3 has been determined, [ 93 ] [ 96 ] [ 97 ] excluding prefiltering and intake/outfall pumping.

claims.claim: The energy intensity of seawater desalination is about 3 kWh per cubic meter (2018), down by a factor of 10 from 20-30 kWh/m3 in 1970.
claims.episode_span: the net electricity demand remains on the order of three to four kilowatt-hours per cubic meter for typical seawater
claims.supporting_quote: The energy intensity of seawater desalination has improved: It is now about 3 kWh/m 3 (in 2018), down by a factor of 10 from 20-30 kWh/m 3 in 1970.

claims.claim: Modern isobaric pressure exchangers transfer the energy in the brine stream to the feed at approximately 98% efficiency.
claims.episode_span: Even with modern isobaric energy-recovery devices that capture 95 percent or more of the pressure energy in the brine stream
claims.supporting_quote: the energy contained in the brine is transferred hydraulically [ 1 ] [ 2 ] and with an efficiency of approximately 98% to the feed.

claims.claim: Reverse-osmosis plants have achieved energy consumption under 2 kWh per cubic meter, within about twice the thermodynamic floor.
claims.episode_span: Modern plants already reach within a few times of that thermodynamic floor on the energy line alone.
claims.supporting_quote: Under 2 kWh/m 3 [ 98 ] has been achieved with reverse osmosis membrane technology, leaving limited scope for further energy reduction, as the reverse osmosis energy consumption in the 1970s was 16 kWh/m 3 .

claims.claim: The Carlsbad seawater RO plant uses about 3.6 kWh per cubic meter of fresh water (~38 MW continuous for 50 million gallons/day).
claims.episode_span: the net electricity demand remains on the order of three to four kilowatt-hours per cubic meter for typical seawater
claims.source_title: Claude "Bud" Lewis Carlsbad Desalination Plant - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: of water per day [ 38 ] ( 0.069 km 3 /a ) with energy use of ~3.6 [ 39 ] kWh for 1 m 3 fresh water

claims.claim: The Carlsbad plant took nearly 14 years to permit, design and build, at a project cost near $1 billion.
claims.episode_span: A large plant is a multi-year construction project whose output does not begin until the entire facility is commissioned.
claims.source_title: Claude "Bud" Lewis Carlsbad Desalination Plant - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: The plant took nearly 14 years to permit, design, and build.

claims.claim: Carlsbad's water is bought under a 30-year Water Purchase Agreement (up to 56,000 acre-feet/yr), i.e. capital is recovered over roughly three decades.
claims.episode_span: Interest and return requirements on that capital are recovered over the plant’s operating life, often twenty to thirty years.
claims.source_title: Seawater Desalination - San Diego County Water Authority
claims.supporting_quote: In November 2012, the Water Authority approved a 30-year Water Purchase Agreement with Poseidon Water for the purchase of up to 56,000 acre-feet of desalinated seawater per year

claims.claim: Carlsbad runs 144 energy recovery devices that cut the reverse-osmosis process's energy use by 46 percent.
claims.episode_span: Even with modern isobaric energy-recovery devices that capture 95 percent or more of the pressure energy in the brine stream
claims.source_title: Seawater Desalination - San Diego County Water Authority
claims.supporting_quote: There are 144 energy recovery devices at work in the plant, reducing the overall energy consumption of the reverse osmosis process by 46 percent.

claims.claim: The PX Pressure Exchanger is an isobaric energy recovery device that reduces desalination energy consumption by up to 60%.
claims.episode_span: Even with modern isobaric energy-recovery devices that capture 95 percent or more of the pressure energy in the brine stream
claims.source_title: PX Q400: Highly Efficient Energy Recovery Device - Energy Recovery
claims.supporting_quote: an isobaric energy recovery device (ERD) that reduces energy consumption by up to 60% in desalination applications.

claims.claim: Carlsbad water was projected at $1,849-2,064 per acre-foot at the plant ($2,014-2,257 delivered), i.e. roughly $1.50-1.85 per cubic meter.
claims.episode_span: A typical large seawater reverse-osmosis facility reports total costs of roughly a dollar or more per cubic meter, with capital recovery among the largest components of that total.
claims.source_title: $734 Million Carlsbad Desalination Project Financing Closes - San Diego County Water Authority
claims.supporting_quote: Water from the plant is expected to cost between $1,849 and $2,064 per acre-foot, depending on how much is purchased.
